sourcedFrom: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) (UNKNOWN — no publication year is printed in the document)
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Steyr Arms's manual for the CL II rifle family, which does not name the Pro Hunter III, so check your variant against it. Steyr Arms USA lists that book as the Pro Hunter III's manual; every step below is quoted from it and stated as generally as the book states it.

The rifle strips to two pieces for cleaning: rifle and bolt. The bolt comes out with the rotary safety set to Lock, and Steyr publishes one step past that — the bolt sleeve comes off and the firing pin assembly slides out, for the rare case when no gunsmith is available. Steyr says complete disassembly of the rifle is usually not needed, and the barrel is always cleaned from the chamber end.

steps.title: Rotary safety to Safe — only the white dot showing
steps.action: This guide follows Steyr Arms's manual for the CL II rifle family, which does not name the Pro Hunter III, so check your variant against it. Point the muzzle somewhere safe and turn the rotary safety on the butt neck backward until it clicks into Safe: only the white dot shows, no red. In Safe the trigger is blocked and the bolt can still be opened, which is what the next steps need. Keep your finger outside the trigger guard throughout.
steps.quote: Move rotary safety in position “Safe“ (Fig. 4 only white dot is visible).
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 9. Loading / unloading — Unloading, printed p.26

steps.title: Magazine out — both snap latches squeezed together
steps.action: Squeeze the two snap latches on either side of the magazine together between thumb and index finger and draw the magazine out while you hold them. Taking the magazine out does nothing to a round already in the chamber, so the next step is not optional.
steps.aside: It is possible that a round may be in the chamber when a loaded or empty magazine is being removed or inserted.
steps.quote: Press the two snap latches at the right and the left of the magazine fully together using thumb and index finger of one hand and remove the magazine while pressing.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 7. Removing the magazine, printed p.21

steps.title: Bolt open and back — chamber proven empty
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt fully back; a chambered cartridge is extracted and thrown clear. Then look into the chamber and the magazine well yourself. If you see brass, stop and clear it before going on.
steps.quote: By opening the bolt handle and retracting the bolt, the cartridge located in the loading chamber of the barrel will be extracted and ejected. Make certain that no cartridge is in the chamber.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 9. Loading / unloading — Unloading, printed p.26

steps.title: Bolt handle turned 70° to the left
steps.action: With the rifle proven empty, take the bolt handle in your right hand and turn it up 70° to the left to unlock the bolt. Steyr recommends taking the bolt out so the barrel can be cleaned properly from the chamber end.
steps.aside: Removal of the bolt is recommended to facilitate proper cleaning of the barrel.
steps.quote: With your right hand, turn bolt handle 70° to the left (unlocking).
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 10. Removing the bolt, printed p.27

steps.title: Rotary safety on to Lock — the gray lock shows
steps.action: With the handle still open, turn the rotary safety backward past Safe until the gray lock snaps out. Steyr's bolt-removal sequence sets the safety to Lock before the bolt is drawn out — follow it in that order.
steps.quote: Move rotary safety to position “Lock“ (Fig. 5 gray lock snaps out).
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 10. Removing the bolt, printed p.27

steps.title: Bolt drawn out by its handle
steps.action: Hold the bolt by its handle and draw it straight back and out of the receiver. Set it down somewhere clean — it goes back in the same way, with the safety at Lock.
steps.quote: Hold bolt by the bolt handle and extract it from the receiver.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 10. Removing the bolt, printed p.27

steps.title: Field strip complete — action stays in the stock
steps.action: Rifle and bolt is the whole field strip. The two screws under the stock hold the action in it, and Steyr says taking the rifle apart further is usually not something the owner needs to do.
steps.quote: Complete disassembly of the rifle by the user usually is not required.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 13. Disassembling the rifle, printed p.30

steps.title: Always from the chamber end, never back through the muzzle
steps.action: Lay the rifle level on a firm surface and work from the chamber end, out through the muzzle. When a patch comes out of the muzzle, take it off the rod — never pull it back through. The muzzle crown is what the rule protects.
steps.aside: Never draw the silk noil or cotton patch back through the barrel after it emerges from the muzzle; rather, remove the noil or patch.
steps.quote: Make sure to always clean the barrel from the chamber to the muzzle.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.39

steps.title: Solvent patch pushed all the way through
steps.action: Fix a clean patch to the patch holder, wet it with bore solvent and push it through the whole bore, then take it off the rod at the muzzle end. Use patches and brushes the right size for the bore — Steyr warns that oversized ones can knock loose the rotary bushing between barrel and receiver, and then the bolt will not go in or lock.
steps.aside: The rotary bushing located between the barrel and the receiver may be dislodged by improper cleaning, including the use of oversized patches or oversized cleaning brushes.
steps.quote: Moisten the patch with bore solvent and push it through the bore completely.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — Cleaning of the bore, printed p.40

steps.title: Bronze brush after the dwell time — never steel
steps.action: Swap the patch holder for a bronze brush of the correct size and push it through the wet bore several times once the solvent has had its dwell time. Steyr's guide is one back-and-forth cycle for every three rounds fired. A steel brush is never used in this barrel.
steps.aside: Never use steel brushes to clean the barrel.
steps.quote: Push a correct size bronze brush a several times through the wet bore after the recommended dwell time.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — Cleaning of the bore, printed p.40

steps.title: Patch until clean, then dry
steps.action: Go back to the patch holder and push patches through chamber and bore until a solvent-wet patch comes out clean, then run a clean dry patch to take out the last of the solvent. If the rifle will be stored a long time or used in damp, corrosive air, oil the bore and chamber lightly.
steps.aside: Slightly oil the bore and chamber, if you store the rifle for a longer period of time or the rifle is used in a corrosive atmosphere.
steps.quote: Remove the remaining bore solvent with a clean and dry patch.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — Cleaning of the bore, printed p.41

steps.title: Heavy fouling past 40 rounds — copper and carbon in turn
steps.action: After more than about 40 rounds, copper shows as a copper-coloured residue at the muzzle and carbon as black between the lands. Steyr's answer is to alternate a copper solvent and a carbon remover, each used as its maker directs, brushing and patching from the chamber end until a fresh wet patch comes through clean.
steps.aside: Heavy fouling deposits increase the pressure inside of the barrel, resulting in hard extractions, loss of accuracy and potentially making the rifle unsafe to use.
steps.quote: For best results alternately use a copper solvent and a carbon remover referring to the recommendation of the solvent manufacturer’s.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — Cleaning of the bore (more than 40 rounds), printed p.41

steps.title: Chamber brushed — then the bore again
steps.action: Clean the chamber with a chamber brush or a section of cleaning rod. Then clean the bore once more, because cleaning the chamber pushes solvent into it.
steps.aside: Always clean the bore after cleaning the chamber to remove bore solvent.
steps.quote: Clean the chamber with a fitting cleaning brush or a cleaning rod section.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — Cleaning of the chamber, printed p.41

steps.title: Surplus solvent wiped out of the receiver
steps.action: Wipe every trace of spare solvent out of the receiver, and off a compensator if the rifle has one. Steyr asks for this after both the chamber and the heavy-fouling clean.
steps.quote: Wipe away all surplus solvent from the receiver and compensator.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — Cleaning of the chamber, printed p.41

steps.title: Outer metal lightly oiled — solvents kept off the synthetics
steps.action: Give the outer metal surfaces a light coat of gun oil after cleaning. Keep solvent-based care products — and insect repellent — off the synthetic stock, because Steyr warns they can change or damage it. A scope mount stays clean and lightly oiled.
steps.aside: The use of gun care products and cleaning agents as well as insect repellents containing solvents may alter or even damage the synthetic parts.
steps.quote: After cleaning slightly oil the outer surfaces of the metal parts with weapon oil.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance — General rifle cleaning, printed p.42

steps.title: Oil out of the bore before you shoot
steps.action: Before the rifle is fired again, run a clean dry patch through bore and chamber to take out any storage oil. Steyr's reason is accuracy: oil left in the bore moves the point of impact.
steps.quote: Before shooting remove the oil from the bore and chamber with a dry and clean patch to avoid a deviation of the point of impact.
steps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 17. Cleaning and maintenance, printed p.41

deepSteps.title: The bolt normally stays closed — this is the exception
deepSteps.action: Steyr's position is that the bolt is lubricated for life at the factory and normally needs no disassembly; an occasional inspection by a Steyr dealer's gunsmith is the routine. The book publishes the bolt strip for special circumstances when no gunsmith is available. Start only with the rifle proven empty and the bolt out of it.
deepSteps.aside: As a rule, occasional inspection by the gunsmith of your franchised STEYR ARMS Dealer should be sufficient to ensure adequate maintenance.
deepSteps.quote: Under normal circumstances, the bolt doesn’t need to be disassembled.
deepSteps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: Catch lever in, bolt sleeve turned clockwise to the click
deepSteps.action: Hold the bolt in your left hand. Press the catch lever in with your right thumb and, at the same time, rotate the bolt sleeve clockwise until it unlocks with an audible click. Clockwise only: Steyr warns that turning the sleeve the other way while dismantling stops the bolt going back into the receiver.
deepSteps.aside: When disassembling, never rotate the bolt sleeve in counterclockwise direction.
deepSteps.quote: Push in catch lever with your right thumb and simultaneously rotate the bolt sleeve clockwise (arrow shows direction of rotation) until it unlocks with an audible click.
deepSteps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: Bolt sleeve off, firing pin assembly out — and that is the end
deepSteps.action: Lift the bolt sleeve off and draw the firing pin assembly out of the bolt. This is as far as Steyr takes the owner; anything further belongs to a gunsmith.
deepSteps.aside: Any further disassembly should be done only by adequately trained and skilled personnel (gunsmith).
deepSteps.quote: Take off bolt sleeve and extract firing pin assembly.
deepSteps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: All bolt parts cleaned and oiled
deepSteps.action: With the bolt open, clean the bolt body, the bolt sleeve and the firing pin assembly, and oil them.
deepSteps.quote: If necessary you can clean and oil all parts of the bolt complete.
deepSteps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt, printed p.31

deepSteps.title: Firing pin assembly back in, lug opposite the handle
deepSteps.action: Hold the bolt in your left hand and slide the firing pin assembly back in, with the firing pin lug lined up directly opposite the bolt handle.
deepSteps.quote: Grip the bolt with your left hand and insert firing pin assembly into bolt with the firing pin lug aligned directly opposite to the bolt handle.
deepSteps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt — Reassembling the bolt, printed p.32

deepSteps.title: Bolt cap on, ratchet lever pressed, turned counterclockwise to lock
deepSteps.action: Slide the bolt cap onto the firing pin lug until it stops, pressing the ratchet lever with your thumb as you do, then rotate the cap counterclockwise until it locks. Stop at the line of alignment — do not turn past it.
deepSteps.aside: Make sure not to turn the bolt cap beyond the line of alignment.
deepSteps.quote: Rotate the bolt cap counterclockwise until it locks into position.
deepSteps.cite: STEYR MANNLICHER CL II Instructions for Use (CL II / CL II SX / Carbon CL II / CL II SX Varmint) — Edition EU 04, 1-BA-6602 (printed on the cover) — 14. Disassembling the bolt — Reassembling the bolt, printed p.32

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Rifle level on a firm surface; bolt out
Always from the chamber end; patch taken off at the muzzle
Solvent patch through, bronze brush after the dwell time, patch until clean
Never use a steel brush in the barrel
Do not use oversized patches or brushes — they can dislodge the rotary bushing
Dry patch to finish; light oil only for storage or a corrosive atmosphere

cleaning.name: CHAMBER & RECEIVER
tasks: Chamber brushed with a fitting brush or rod section
Bore cleaned again after the chamber
Surplus solvent wiped out of the receiver

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Outer metal surfaces lightly oiled with gun oil
Do not let solvent-based products or insect repellent reach the synthetic parts
Scope mount kept clean and lightly oiled
Storage oil removed from bore and chamber before shooting

reassembly: Magazine out (or locked in its second position) and the rifle unloaded before the bolt goes back.
Rotary safety at Lock; bolt held by its handle and slid into the receiver, turned so the handle runs into its slot.
Safety moved to the Firing position and the bolt handle locked down while the trigger is held back, so the firing pin is not cocked — the indicator pin at the rear of the bolt sleeve disappears.
Rotary safety back to Safe, then a function check before any ammunition.
fncheck: Rifle empty, magazine out, muzzle safe. Work the bolt several times — it should open, run and lock down without binding; if it will not go in or lock, the rotary bushing may have been dislodged and the rifle goes to a Steyr dealer. Check the rotary safety: at Safe only the white dot shows and the bolt still opens; at Lock the gray lock shows and the bolt stays shut. If any safety proves ineffective, Steyr says the rifle is not to be used until authorized personnel have repaired and checked it.
